habelia.observations: Independently read species diagnosis, cephalic appendages, trunk and tail sections, plus correction. Actual Fig1 D-G depicts morph A; A-C/H are morph B. Fig3 is an interpretive drawing, not specimen evidence. Species description gives 12 trunk segments, first five with robust walking endopods; posterior 6-12 exopods. Family diagnosis says eight post-thoracic segments inconsistently. This remains disclosed rather than silently harmonized. Correction concerns Thelxiope tergites and H.optata species terminology, not a new Habelia count. Final model has five paired basal gnathobase pads with separate forward raptorial/endite branches and fine lateral exopods; microscopic dentition is simplified.

alalcomenaeus.observations: Read actual ROM morphology and Aria2015 Eyes discussion. The latter treats two mushroom-shaped median eyes as likely leanchoiliid anatomy while historical fifth Alalcomenaeus eye evidence remains unclear. ROM45616 and USNM155658 specimen pixels show shield, repeated trunk and broad spatulate tail. Leanchoilia comparator has pointed/lanceolate terminal construction. Final broad unpaired spatula, enclosed flanks and short peduncles provide visible structural separation. No CNS reconstruction accepted. The 1999 Wiley page returned 403 in this review; historical uncertainty is corroborated by the accessible 2015 primary paper, not falsely claimed to have read full1999.

plenocaris.observations: Actual ROM61125 and USNM57700 specimen pixels independently inspected; short anterior shield, long limbless ringed abdomen and paired broad caudal paddles supported. Museum morphology specifies approximately ten antennal segments each bearing a ventral spine, 2-4 front leg pairs and 13 abdomen rings. Three modeled leg pairs are a disclosed choice, not fossil certainty. Fine head/limb anatomy is weakly known and full1974 monograph was not obtained/read. Perspicaris comparative specimen shows much larger enclosing valve region and narrow forked tail. Final Plenocaris is structurally distinct, but topological subdivision alone does not depict segmented antennae. This is a frozen visible-feature failure, not a new hard dimensional gate.

nectocaris.observations: Independently read 2025 diagnosis, genus distinction and tentative feeding discussion in local full PDF text. Personally viewed actual N.pteryx Fig6G-H and J/L/M, with I/K/N recognized as interpretive overlays. A-F concern N.latus, not N.pteryx; O/P are schematics, not specimen pixels. ROM59658 and59660 external fossils inspected separately. Full-length fin rays, no distinct caudal fin region, stalked eyes, forward antennae and flared tube mouth match final. Internal jaws not external ornaments; stem-chaetognath interpretation and tentative suction replace obsolete cephalopod/jet certainty. Fin ridge count, palette and thickness remain artistic.
